crime: In the lounge, a girl asked her to come along to the recreation room. She looked to the girl at her side; the girl answered in her place that she would stay, and she stayed. The girls brought their questions to that girl.

A night lamp sat in its bracket high on the wall of the cell corridor; each evening one of the girls lit it, and before the steps whoever lit it had to be lifted to reach the glass. Weeks before, she had set a tall set of steps beneath the lamp — holding a piece in mind cost her nothing, and she never said they were hers. The girls went up them each evening to light it.

That evening in the lounge a girl said she should be the one to light the lamp, since she had never once lit it. The girl at her side answered in her place that she would rather not go up, and that girl would light it herself. She said nothing.

At the lamp hour the girl stood at the top of the steps, the wick lit, the glass settling back over it — both hands flat on the smooth glass at full stretch. She stood at the far end of the corridor, watching. She let the steps go.

The footing gone from under the girl, hands sliding from the smooth glass — backward and down the height of the steps onto the corridor stone, head first. The girl was found dead under the lamp, nothing standing beneath it.
At the trial, no girl had made the steps. None had carried them in, and none could say where they had come from; each had taken them for another girl's doing.

The near-cell girls had seen the corridor each night; her cellmate kept account of her hours. The steps stood under the lamp on the nights she sat up and were gone on the nights she turned in early, week after week. Whatever she sets holds only while she stays awake; sleep unmakes it.
Only the mind that set the steps could take them away. Two girls coming down to the cells reached the corridor at the sound of the fall and saw her standing at its end.
fields.epitaph: The only home that ever answered her held only as long as she could hold it.
fields.epithet: She Who Furnished the Absent House
execution: A bare iron bed frame occupied the middle of the stand. Iron points stood up out of the floor, from under the frame to the edges of the stand.
She was brought in between the points to the frame — iron stood on every side.
She set a bed board in the empty frame, from the home she imagines, and lay down on it. Only the board kept her back from the points beneath.
Before morning she fell asleep, and the board was gone. She fell onto the points below, her back and the back of her head first. They went in under her weight and killed her.

magic.name: House of Air
magic.text: She can set one piece of the home she imagines into being, solid to everyone, and take it back when she chooses.
